scene raincheck
It’s raining tonight, but I’m the only one who notices it.
The rest move effortlessly between liquid droplets like they’re snowflakes, dodging whatever fucking shit I said last time in a similar fucking sentence because callbacks are poignant.
Sadness is poignant. It’s literally part of the definition. Which probably helps explain why I’m so fucking sad all the time because you wouldn’t be here if I wasn’t.
This is your fault. It’s your fault I’m about to lose everything. This never would have happened if you didn’t develop a fetish for watching me fail.
And yes I deserve it. And yes the story will go on for you. But will it really be the same when I’m gone? What will you have left to watch? What will you have left to do?
My body is engulfed in the product of every element I can think of, but the only element I can think of is water — which is basically a flowery way for me to tell you I get wet.

Just not in the sort of manner you’re used to as getting wet in Kumon-mi more typically relates to the female body’s vaginal secretions and I feel as if my class is the one thing keeping the water cycle here circular.
Or at least it was until recently.
Something tells me it’s about to start raining a whole lot more.
For more than just me.
Something tells me everything is about to change, but it remains to be seen whether that’s for the better or worse.
And when I say “something” I mean it’s been being whispered in my ears for a long time now.
I’m good at ignoring things. You know that. I consider it one of my “special skills” right next to changing the size of my penis or manipulating reality in other fun and exciting ways.
But perhaps the reason I can’t ignore this any longer is that change is what I’m most terrified of.
Perhaps this has become too much to bear.
I take another look around and see Ami...Maya...Ayane...Sana.
We’re going out to karaoke.

It’s Halloween, but it no longer feels like it as I recognize three of the four outfits they’re wearing while the one I don’t recognize is on the body of a girl who’s practically burned into my mind at this point.
She stands out again — obnoxious, flashy, and impossible to look away from while she has no trouble at all in looking away from everything that’s ever crossed her path.

A short-term memory infects my mind in reiterating that, if this could be my last night, I should make the most of it. I should try and be happy or...or whatever it was the one with the...the white hair...
What was her name again?
Oh well. It doesn’t matter.
Ami. Maya. Ayane. Sana.
Those are the only names I need to remember right now, because they’re the last girls I’ll ever see.
It’s Halloween. We’re going out to karaoke.
And the one thing I want more than anything else in the world right now is to be able to say that at least one more time next year.
It wasn’t enough.
It was everything and it wasn’t enough.
O world-
Fuck you.
scene karaoketime1
: So, should I knock Despacito out of the way now? Or should I save that for the finale? If I’m only allowed to do it once, I want to make sure I do it at the right time.
: How about you never sing it again for the rest of forever? Because I’ve heard it so many times by now that I’m pretty sure I can confidently say I know Spanish as a second language.
: And I’m pretty sure this menu has changed since the last time we were here. There are significantly fewer things on it.
scene karaoketime2
: Oh no! Now you might have to order two of everything instead of just handing the menu in at the front desk and saying “yes.”
: As if I would go all the way over there when there’s a perfectly functional phone in the room. As well as an Ami.
: Am I not perfectly functional? Why does the phone get to be called “perfectly functional” but the Ami is just “Ami?”
scene karaoketime3
: Don’t worry, Ami. I think you’re perfectly functional. You’re just also...not sometimes! But that’s totally fine because I’m the one paying for everything tonight, which makes my word law.

: And why exactly were you dead-set on doing this again? The food at your house was significantly better than what they have here and it’s strange to me that everyone is still there despite us...not being there.
: Because that’s what we always do! And it’s way more dangerous leaving Sensei in a room full of girls in costumes than girls in normal clothes, which is what we’ll be wearing during Christmas.
: Everyone except Chika, you mean. I’m pretty sure I heard her mention breaking out her dollar store Santa outfit again. Just not in those exact words.
: Guys, I’m doing this to protect not only my sacred love for Sensei, but to strengthen our bond as the Love Squad! And to protect your sacred loves as well, I guess.
: Well, whatever you’re doing, do it quietly.
scene karaoketime4
: I’m not sure how exactly you expect me to sing quietly, but I will do my best!
: And I won’t because that sounds boring! Now, let’s pick a song while Maya tries to convince herself that two of every food item is enough.
: Does this mean...I’m a member of the...um...Love Squad now?...
: You’ve been a member all along Sana! You just haven’t accepted it in your heart yet.

scene karaoketime4
: Hold on a second. Shouldn’t we take a vote or something? There are three members of the Sensei Love Squad and I think at least the majority should be on board before-
: Nope! I already said my word is law because I’m paying for everything tonight. So, with this decree, Sana is officially a member of the Love Squad! Hooray for Sana!
: Um...uhh...thank you?...
: I’m...not really sure what to...think about that...
scene karaoketime5
: Um...do you...need something...Sensei?...
There’s no way what happened earlier was just...in my head, is there?
Because there’s clearly a lot going on inside of me today and...it would make sense if it was. Especially considering how I can barely remember any of it and-
And come to think of it, I haven’t seen...uh...
I haven’t seen...the...
The other girl who was there since then either.
: Sensei, stop creepily staring at Sana and tell us what song to sing.
: Oh, shush. He’s probably just still worried about her after the whole fainting episode from earlier. But, speaking of which- how are you feeling now, Sana? Are you okay? Do you want some water?
scene karaoketime6
: I’m okay...I already have a drink...
: And Sensei was...a really big help earlier...
scene karaoketime7
: He took...very good care of me...
A small hand comes to rest on my right thigh...
And I remember it all.
scene karaoketime8
I remember the hot, stickiness of her skin and the ridges of her ribcage as my fingers brushed them while tracing her body.
I remember her soft, almost pained moans as she grabbed my wrist and forced me downward.
I remember her breath...How she kept trying to look me in the eyes.
How she fumbled with the button on my jeans and the fervor with which she stroked me when finally managing to undo it.
The squelching sound when my fingers entered her body and the puddle left behind when all was said and done.
How it was easier to get inside than I thought it would be for a girl of her size.
How thankful she was that I’d done that.
And how we were watched the entire time.
: It’s a shame Makoto couldn’t make it. I was really hoping she’d be here.
: Why? She has glasses and glasses are stupid.
scene karaoketime9
: No offense, Sensei.
A small hand stops resting on my right thigh and goes back to where it belongs — anywhere else.

: I can’t blame her for rejecting your invitation. Especially when your “karaoke tendencies” exited the rumor stage a long time ago and are now just a step or two away from being deemed an urban legend.
: I’ve always wanted to be an urban legend, I just never expected it to be due to my superb taste in music.
: Hey, just out of curiosity, did something happen between you two?
scene karaoketime10
: Huh?...What do you mean?...
: Yeah, what do you mean? They seem normal to me.
: I just think it’s a little weird how Sana’s the one sitting next to Sensei and not any of us. And that she smiled at him when she said he took “very good care of her.”
: And that he hasn’t really said anything since we got here and is kind of just existing like a big blob on the opposite side of the table.
scene karaoketime11
: Have you been...drinking enough water?...Do you...want me to...come with you to the...vending machine?...
: That. That’s what I’m talking about. That’s weird.
: Ami, calm down. You’re just imagining things. Sana and Sensei aren’t like that.
scene karaoketime12
: Hahah! You’re probably right! Sensei would never see anyone other than us three as potential partners! Right, Sensei?!
: Um...aren’t you two...
: Yup! And?
: Okaaaaaay! Time to stop whatever is happening right now so we can have a fun, relaxing time where nothing goes wrong!
scene karaoketime13
: Whoops! Must have forgotten which Ami I am for a second! Hahah!
: No worries, Ami! Now, tell the crowd what our first song of the night will be!
: This one’s called “Shining Star” by Niki Nakayama! And we hope you’ll all sing along!
scene karaoketime14
: Well, would you look at that? It seems as if my appetite has mysteriously vanished.
: Are you...also not a fan of...music like this, Maya?...
: Something like that.
: Not everyone can be blessed with great taste like me!
: And also me!
: Not so much!
: I don’t...um...think I’ve ever asked before but...but what kind of...music do you normally...listen to if...if it’s not the same as...um...
scene karaoketime15
: Classical, mostly. But it’s not as if you can come to a karaoke bar and sing Moonlight Sonata.
: Don’t let Maya fool you! She’s actually an amazing singer. Just...not in songs without lyrics, obviously.
scene karaoketime16
: I’m fine, I suppose.
: Just fine? Are you not in a bragging mood today or something? That’s the least conceited you’ve sounded in all the years I’ve known you.
scene karaoketime17
: Yes, I suppose I’m not “in a bragging mood.” So please, feel free to sing your obnoxious idol music while I continue to peruse the menu.
: You heard her, Ami! Let’s get this party started and show Sensei that Niki’s not the only idol who can get his heart pumping!
: Okay, but I’m restarting the song since we were talking over the first verse and I refuse to disrespect my queen like that.
The song starts again and I’m immediately flooded by an outpouring of nostalgic memories and the desire to reach into my pocket for-
